analysis.title: Industrial Metals Weekly: Copper prices down with the market, but Chinese physical indicators tighten
key_insights: Following the Democratic sweep in the US midterms, copper fell to ~$6.40/lb from ~$6.60/lb on lower tariff odds and potentially weaker AI data centre demand, tracking broader market sentiment. Copper equities mirrored the decline and valuations remain at historical discounts relative to spot.

The Chinese physical copper market continued to tighten on weaker Chilean production. The Yangshan premium hit a record $230/t while Trafigura bought large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia with Chinese inventory already low.
Shanghai copper inventories fell to 33,848mt (-10,764kt w/w) on Friday as the physical market in China tightens.
SMM reports eleven smelters underwent maintenance during the month, with an estimated production impact of 103,200 tonnes. Domestic copper cathode output fell 3.03% m/m to 1,086,700 tonnes.
Weekly moves: copper -3.0% to $6.33/lb, nickel +5.5% to $7.30/lb, zinc -4.5% to $1.71/lb. Met coal -1.2% to $282.70/mt, iron ore +2.9% to $93.30/dmt.

Q3 copper producer results benefited from strong metal prices, but weather and ramp-up issues led to downward guidance revisions across the board. All five copper producers trimmed 2026 guidance, with an average production miss of 5.9% and guidance reductions averaging 3.8%.

Extreme weather was the main cause of the misses, hitting Lundin's Caserones, Capstone's Pinto Valley and Chilean operations, and Freeport's US mines. Lower grades pushed higher-grade access into 2027. Ivanhoe's quarter was hurt by ramp-up delays at Kakula. Capstone did not cut guidance but expects production at the low end.
Hudbay reports Thursday before the open, ending a generally challenging Q3 for copper producers under RBC coverage.
RBC updated Lundin estimates after Q3 with no change to the Sector Perform rating or C$47.00 price target. 2026E adjusted EPS is $1.38 (previously $1.52) and 2027E is $1.61 (previously $1.60).
North American copper producers trade at 0.7x P/NAV against a 10-year average of 0.9x and a 3-year average of 1.0x. Global diversifieds trade at 1.0x against a 10-year average of 0.9x.
Copper equities have lagged copper on a year-to-date basis. Copper equities are -7.0% YTD against copper at +8.3%, per the asset performance chart.
RBC copper price deck: $6.13/lb in 2026E, $6.00/lb in 2027E and 2028E, and $5.00/lb long-term.

sector_views.rationale: Prices fell on lower tariff odds and possible weaker AI data centre demand, while the Chinese physical market tightens on low inventory and weaker Chilean output.
Valuations remain at historical discounts relative to spot, while Q3 guidance cuts across all five covered producers weigh on sentiment.

earnings_insights: All five covered copper producers trimmed 2026 guidance in Q3, with an average production miss of 5.9% and guidance reductions averaging 3.8%. Ivanhoe and Freeport pre-released production and are excluded from the Q3 production average.
Hudbay reports Q3 on Thursday before the open (not yet reported). It is the last covered copper producer to report this season.
Lundin Q3 adjusted EPS estimate is 0.32E, previously 0.56E under the old Q3 line. Quarterly estimates run Q1 2026 0.33A, Q2 0.30E, Q3 0.32E, Q4 0.45E.
Lundin FY2026E adjusted diluted EPS is $1.38 (previously $1.52). FY2027E is $1.61 (previously $1.60). FY2028E is $1.23. FY2026E adjusted EBITDA is $2,627.8M (previously $2,870.6M).

Lundin catalysts: Vicuña district FID in 2026, ball mill commissioning at Chapada and Caserones in 2027, Saúva first ore in 2029, and the Candelaria Franco-Nevada stream step-down from 68% to 40% in Q1 2027, adding ~$56-90M in annual FCF.

tension_points.bull_case: The Chinese physical market is tightening, with Shanghai inventories at 33,848mt, a record Yangshan premium of $230/t, weaker Chilean production and Trafigura buying large volumes. Copper equities trade at historical discounts to spot.
tension_points.bear_case: Copper fell to ~$6.40/lb on lower tariff odds after the US midterms and potentially weaker AI data centre demand, following broader market sentiment. Q3 guidance cuts across all five covered producers add pressure on the equities.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hudbay's Thursday Q3 report is the next test of whether the guidance-cut trend continues.
